description: 5mΩ 3W Current Sense Resistor ±1% ±50ppm/℃ 2512 Chip Resistor - Surface Mount RoHS

provenance.pins: two-terminal current-sense resistor, 2512. Pin numbers from the EasyEDA Pro symbol via tools/eda.py; the element is symmetrical and carries no polarity.

designVerdict: SELECTED as R1 - the low-side current-sense shunt in the shared LED return.
notes: 5 mOhm, 1%, 3 W, +-50 ppm/C, 2512. Same tolerance and temperature coefficient as the 10 mOhm C7419995 it replaces, with a higher power rating and 22x the stock.

SIZED AGAINST THE RETURN, NOT THE CONTRACT. The INA226's differential input is +-81.92 mV, so full scale here is 16.4 A. That has to cover what the shared return can actually carry - the 8.0 A full-white flash and the 11.1 A the two TPS16630 eFuses pass before either limits - not the 5 A PD contract. At 10 mOhm full scale was 8.19 A: normal operation at 98% of range with the whole fault band above it.

Resolution is 0.5 mA per LSB at the INA226's 2.5 uV, so about 10,000 counts at a 5 A contract current. Halving the shunt halved the counts and they are still ample; it also halved the LED_RTN ground lift to 25 mV at 5 A and the dissipation to 0.125 W, against 0.62 W at the 11.1 A fault limit in a 3 W part.
KELVIN CONNECTION. It carries the full return current, so the two sense traces are a layout item, not a routing afterthought - take them from the pad ends.
